Most of it, yes — and honestly the everyday backbone feels really solid. Saving fast with the details filled in, finding things by word or by the address, my own labels, the read-later list that empties as I go, the preserved copies (including real PDFs), no duplicates, fixing up details, deleting, and the gentle put-away-and-restore — all of that is exactly the day-to-day I pictured. I'm pleased with it.

Since you're asking whether it's a *complete* everyday flow, though, there are a few things that feel like part of normal daily use that I don't think we've actually walked through yet:

- **Actually opening a saved link.** The whole reason I save these is to go back to them, so clicking a bookmark in my list should take me to the real website. I don't think we ever confirmed that basic bit.
- **Ordering my list.** Once I've got a lot saved, I'd want to arrange it — newest first, or oldest, or by name — rather than being stuck with one fixed order.
- **Doing something to several at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd like to select a handful of bookmarks and, say, put a label on all of them, mark them read, put them away, or delete them together, instead of one at a time.
- **Sharpening a search.** Beyond plain words, I'd expect to narrow to a particular label right in the search, combine a couple of conditions (this *and* that, or *not* that), and search an exact phrase when I remember the precise wording.

None of that undoes what you've shown — the pieces so far are right. I'd just want those rounded in before I'd call it my complete everyday flow. Can we work through them? And yes, thank you for keeping the personal-notes idea (and searching those notes) on the list for later.
